summary:
# NOTES: "THE HOUSE 'ROUND THE CORNER" by Gordon Holmes (Louis Tracy), 1919, Grosset & Dunlap. Single book.

## Front matter
Proofreading/Gutenberg header. Contents: I Wherein the House Receives a New Tenant; II Showing How Even a House May Have a Way of Its Own; III A Midnight Seance; IV Showing How Explanations Do Not Always Explain; V Gathering Clouds; VI The Storm Breaks; VII A Faint-Hearted Ally; VIII Wherein Percy Whittaker Proves Himself a Man of Action; IX Showing the Real Strength of an Illusion; X Armathwaite States a Case; XI Preparations for Battle; XII The Dawn of a Black Friday; XIII Deus Ex Machina; XIV In Which the Area Widens; XV The Laying of the Ghost.

## Ch I
- Train reaches Nuttonby (North Riding, Yorkshire; 3,005 inhabitants in 1911 census, +2 since 1901). Wednesday = market day, police-court day, Board of Guardians day.
- Stranger (later Robert Armathwaite; real name Sir Robert Dalrymple, K.C.S.I.): tall, sparse, tweeds, deer-stalker cap, fishing rods, pannier, three heavy book boxes ("Books"), one bag. Tickets: first class from York; "York, from King's Cross" and "Nuttonby, from York" labels.
- Porter (brown-tinted, "By gum!", "Wu-Wu-Walker's is straight up"); pert ticket youth. Porter tipped half a crown.
- Walker & Son, auctioneers, land valuers, house agents, next to Red Lion, half-way up main street. Son: young Walker ("nut", sporting paper, cigarette), first name James ("Jim"). Father James Walker senior, bald, pursed lips. Office has huge sale poster for "spacious mansion, with well-timbered park" put up five years earlier.
- Elmdale: 8 miles from Nuttonby, on edge of moor, ~40 houses, beck with trout (4 oz–½ lb), 600 ft above sea level. The Grange (stone, square, portico, stone-slab roof, Jacobean grate in dining-room, 5 bedrooms, garden with spring-fed well, oaken rafters, 17th-century). Furnished. Asking £60/yr.
- History told by Walker senior: Mr Stephen Garth, "some sort of professor", lived with wife and daughter (beauty, Marguérite "Meg"). June two years earlier, Mrs Garth and girl left by train from Nuttonby (governess car, trap sent back). Garth hanged himself beside grandfather clock in hall. Villagers see ghost in June: setting sun through stained-glass window on half landing casts shadow. Last tenant: Sheffield family, Mrs Wilkins (saw ghost, threatened action). Solicitors Holloway & Dobb (Nuttonby) lack Garths' whereabouts.
- Armathwaite: ex-Indian Political officer ("since I left India"), offers quarter's rent; yearly tenancy, 3 months' notice; bank check in 3 days. Bank opposite Walker's office. Elder Walker: "Some houses have an attraction for queer folk."
- Walker drives Armathwaite (11:30 a.m.) in dog-cart to Elmdale via station (collects bag and parcels). Cigar "worth a bob". Walker explains "footed" sheep and fishing rights (Burt, etc.).
- Mrs Jackson (cottage, keys) and daughter Betty (apple-cheeked, 22) panic; Jim snatches keys from hook.

## Ch II
- Walker opens Grange; inventory: seven missing valuable articles found piled on library table with books (~800 volumes). Armathwaite brought ~200 books. Oil lamps, coal, wood left by Mrs Wilkins.
- Best bedroom (south-east). Attic via trap-door in lobby; Walker shoots bolt on it (later imprisons Meg).
- Armathwaite pays: rent £15, fee 2 guineas, conveyance 1 guinea = £18 3s. Walker sent back with cigar and voucher for boxes.
- Armathwaite roams moor, follows beck to source. Sees Jacksons with ladder peer into his bedroom. Visits Mrs Jackson; asks for milk, butter, eggs; spotted spare key (Betty startled).
- Night: booby-trap gong crashes ~11:30 p.m.; Betty flees. Knocks from attic trap-door. Armathwaite has automatic pistol and electric torch.

## Ch III
- Girl in attic: silk stockings, gray flannel trousers, heather fisherman's hat, borrowed clothes of Percy Whittaker (Cheshire friend's brother). She sneaks into Elmdale on foot 14 miles over moor, from Leyburn station; breakfasted York; lodging with friend in Cheshire.
- Eats boiled eggs in dining-room (cruet, pepper). Father "dad" = food theorist. Armathwaite deduces she is Marguérite Garth but she says father alive; her name Meg. Mackintosh and lady's hat left in hall.
- Says Mrs Garth and she stay away; Mr Garth is "Stephen Ogilvey" (folk-lore author). Letter: she came for books. Armathwaite asks her to leave; she agrees.
- Meg knocks on Jacksons' window; no answer; Armathwaite sends her back in: "I told you so."

## Ch IV
- Morning: Armathwaite explains to Betty; Betty's account: Garth paid off gardener, dismissed maids; Betty found him; Mrs Jackson found body; policeman Leadbitter cut him down; Dr. Scaife; Mr Benson rode to Bellerby; coroner's letter "To the Coroner" laid at clock foot. Mrs Garth & Meg went to France (Paris/Quimper).
- Armathwaite decides: Meg must be sent away believing father alive. Jacksons sworn to silence.
- Breakfast: "Bob" and "Meg" ("cousinship"). Meg's surname now Ogilvey (legacy). Meg's pen-name "Stephen Ogilvey" recognized. Armathwaite: "I thought you were married." Coffee.
- Tom Bland (Nuttonby carrier, Tuesdays/Thursdays/Saturdays) sees Meg at window. Armathwaite insists she is "Meg Ogilvey".

## Ch V
- Bland delivers boxes; Armathwaite pays 16s less 6s (10s total?) plus florin. Bland: "Miss Meg?" Armathwaite: "Miss Marguérite Ogilvey".
- Meg wants to leave via moor on foot; Armathwaite insists on escorting. Discusses Frazer's Golden Bough, Mannhardt, cat's cradle, Jatakas and Panchatantras.
- P.C. Leadbitter (Bellerby, Gordon Highlanders, Tirah medal, Dargai) at porch; Armathwaite says he was at Dargai in "Politicals". Leadbitter knew Garth, found body two days dead; garden ruined ("Begonia Smith" former gardener).
- Leadbitter tells Sir Berkeley Hutton (who goes to see Armathwaite).
- Mrs Jackson and Betty tell Meg about Cornwall; "Miggles" postman; Leyburn train at 7 p.m.; Armathwaite refuses to let her go alone; "mem-sahib" joke. Meg says Percy Whittaker proposed.
- Miggles/Farmer Burt: fishing permission given; Burt to call Saturday. James Walker drives into Elmdale; Armathwaite damns him.

## Ch VI
- Walker confronts Meg; Armathwaite arrives. Walker's remarks about Garth's death; Armathwaite throws Walker out, kicks him down path.
- Meg recovers, Betty, Mrs Jackson. Armathwaite promises to clear matters.
- Meg and Armathwaite walk on moor; he explains everything. They see a man sitting: Percy Whittaker.

## Ch VII
- Percy Whittaker: thin patent-leather shoes, portmanteau weighing "a ton", walked from Leyburn; sent by sister Edie (Mrs Suarez, widow, Calcutta merchant's wife, Whittakers are Anglo-Indians/Eurasian).
- Dad's letter: asks Meg to find "Basque Legends" by Wentworth Webster (1877, 1879) in Chester bookshops.
- Newspaper: Nuttonby Gazette, 22 June two years ago: inquest at Fox and Hounds, Elmdale. Coroner Mr Hill (solicitor). Dr Scaife (Bellerby) doubted cause of death ("apoplexy"; no organic disease). Verdict: "Suicide, while in a state of unsound mind." Interment at Bellerby churchyard. Letter from Garth: incurable disease.
- Percy: suspicious of Armathwaite; wants to send telegram to Edie.

## Ch VIII
- Percy goes to Thompson's shop (opposite Fox and Hounds) to telegraph; Meg tells Armathwaite about Quimper, Warleggan (Cornwall), Paris, Basque songs.
- Armathwaite theorizes; Meg denies; Armathwaite tells of killing men in fair fight (Usman Khel, Nas'r-ulla Khan).
- Meg asks Armathwaite to help, she'll save father; Armathwaite holds her, Percy sees them through window.
- Percy has telegraphed Edie: "Meg greatly disturbed by rumors ... Telegraph her mother at once." Percy says Armathwaite hired? (no)
- Armathwaite goes to village; Meg stays. Percy: "I've stopped those two from billing and cooing."

## Ch IX
- Armathwaite gets Burt's cob and boy; sends telegram to York garage: car for one week, arrive noon Friday, £10 guarantee. Signed "ARMATHWAITE, The Grange, Elmdale, viâ Bellerby".
- Plan: deny Garth alive; Meg's statement a joke.
- Dinner; Armathwaite tells Meg plan. Percy falls downstairs when stained-glass shadow appears (Black Prince, raven-crested helm; malevolent face with empty eye sockets); Percy sprains right ankle.
- Dr Scaife sent for. Burt: window's history; Mrs Ogilvey (Faulkner family) had child there; Faulkner drunkard fell down stairs. Holand Castle; Black Prince; Faulkner (pirate) shot Black Prince's eyes.

## Ch X
- Armathwaite and Meg dine; Meg's plan: mother should not come. Dr Scaife arrives; Meg says "Uncle Ferdie". Scaife recognizes Meg; Armathwaite rebandages Percy; Scaife gives Percy bromide.
- Armathwaite's theory (A–G) about Garth's ruse; Mrs Garth/Ogilvey.
- Scottish Criminal Trials book: statute of James I against evil spirits.
- Armathwaite says he will marry Meg.

## Ch XI
- Walker to Dobb (solicitor, Holloway & Dobb). Dobb: "Mrs Ogilvey"; Walker tells Dobb Meg says father alive.
- Walker tells father and Mr Banks (Nuttonby Gazette, Banks: proprietor/editor/manager). Walker reveals "Armathwaite".
- Dobb's telegram from "SIGMATIC" (India Office) about "passing under the name of Robert Armathwaite".

## Ch XII
- Friday morning, 19th (anniversary). Armathwaite studies Black Prince face. Percy wakes; Armathwaite & Percy.
- Begonia Smith (gardener; ex-gardener, "Begonia Smith") offers to restore garden; tells Black Prince/Faulkner legend.
- Meg comes down; Percy proposes forcibly: must marry him or he will have father arrested.
- Meg flees; Betty and Mrs Jackson talk.

## Ch XIII
- Meg gone (moor road toward Leyburn; left at 9:10 by clock). Armathwaite sends Betty for breakfast; Smith's gang. Telegrams: from Mrs Ogilvey (Tavistock): "Arriving to-night if possible. Don't take any action until I am with you.—MOTHER."
- Armathwaite threatens Percy; smashes stained glass window with fist (glass shatters; oval of blue sky through visor).
- Mrs Jackson: "They've long wanted a man i' this house."
- Armathwaite rides bicycle, finds Meg on moor road; they embrace, "Bob dear", declares love.
- Motor car from York (chauffeur Storr); Armathwaite plans Meg to meet mother at York.

## Ch XIV
- Armathwaite sends Meg to York in car; realises he hasn't told his true name.
- Sir Berkeley Hutton ("Baluchi Bob", "Mollie" = Lady Hutton; "the Pup" = son) identifies him as Sir Robert Dalrymple.
- Morand (India Office): Maharajah of Barapur assassinated; Chalwar Singh; Muncherji; Dalrymple reinstated; deputy Mortimer Collins.
- Dalrymple moved: "my mother's name, Armathwaite".
- Dr Scaife and nurse bring Percy; Percy insists on being taken away.

## Ch XV
- Dalrymple carries Percy back. Conclave: Hutton, Dobb, police superintendent, inspector, Banks; promised report at 2 p.m. next day.
- Percy gives up threat.
- Meg telegram: "All is well. Father leaves for York to-night..." Expect 10 o'clock.
- Dalrymple moves the grandfather clock, ending the ghost.
- Morning: Stephen Garth arrives in car. Smith: "I'm not so dead as you thought me!"
- Stephen Garth's confession: real name Ogilvey; brother James Ogilvey (Birmingham bank embezzlement, transported, arrested in France); died of apoplexy in the Grange after quarrel over money; Garth tied body to hook under shadow; wrote letter to coroner; resumed name Garth; wife Mrs Ogilvey; daughter Meg.
- Ending: Black Prince restored; Walkers see Sir Robert and Lady Dalrymple drive past en route to Paris; "Who'd ha' thought ... the marriage of Meg Garth to Sir Robert Dalrymple?" "Well, I didn't, for one!" said the son gloomily. THE END.
- Trailing back matter: advertisements for Zane Grey, Mary Roberts Rinehart, Booth Tarkington, Kathleen Norris, Sewell Ford, William MacLeod Raine novels (not part of story).
